title: Simultaneous compact descent of pointwise pushout data
statement:
Work in a fixed universe. Let $\kappa$ be uncountable regular and let $\mathcal A$ be an ordinary locally $\kappa$-presentable category with small Hom sets and colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. This means every object is a small $\kappa$-filtered colimit of a small family of $\kappa$-presentable objects; $\kappa$-presentable means that the ordinary Hom functor preserves such colimits, regular means unions of fewer than $\kappa$ sets of size less than $\kappa$ have size less than $\kappa$, and $\kappa$-filtered means every diagram with fewer than $\kappa$ morphisms admits a cocone. Let $D$ have fewer than $\kappa$ morphisms. Assume every $D$-diagram in $\mathcal A$ is a small $\kappa$-filtered colimit of pointwise $\kappa$-presentable diagrams, and that finite colimits of $\kappa$-presentable objects of $\mathcal A$ are $\kappa$-presentable.

Let $f:F\to G$ be a natural transformation such that for every $d$ there is a pushout square with top $u_d:P_d\to Q_d$, bottom $f(d):F(d)\to G(d)$, and left $a_d:P_d\to F(d)$, where $P_d,Q_d$ are $\kappa$-presentable. The arrows $u_d$ and $a_d$ are not required to form natural transformations. Then there exist diagrams $F_0,G_0$, a natural transformation $h:F_0\to G_0$ and a map $F_0\to F$ such that $f$ is the pushout of $h$ along this map in $\operatorname{Fun}(D,\mathcal A)$, both $F_0,G_0$ are pointwise $\kappa$-presentable, and for every $d$, $h(d)$ is a pushout of the same specified $u_d$ along a map $P_d\to F_0(d)$ factoring $a_d$. No monomorphism assumption on $u_d$, $f(d)$, or the filtered transition maps is imposed.

proof.text: Choose the small $\kappa$-filtered presentation of $F$ by pointwise $\kappa$-presentable diagrams assumed in the statement. Apply [lem-coef-cardinal-filtered-poset-reindex] to its indexing category and obtain $F=\varinjlim_{t\in T}F_t$ with $T$ a small $\kappa$-filtered poset. This is also a pointwise colimit: form the colimit of the values at each $d$; an arrow of $D$ induces a map of these colimits by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Uniqueness makes those maps preserve identities and composition. A cocone to any diagram is then exactly its compatible component cocones, so this pointwise construction has the functor-category colimit universal property and identifies with the specified $F$. Write $v_{st}:F_s\to F_t$ and $x_t:F_t\to F$ for the transition and cocone maps.

source.place: Lemma A.3.3.17, first paragraph, with the poset-reindexing input made explicit

proof.text: The compactness arguments below have the following explicit meaning. For a $\kappa$-presentable $K$ and a small $\kappa$-filtered diagram $Z_t$ with colimit $Z$, the definition in the statement identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(K,Z)$ with $\varinjlim_t\operatorname{Hom}(K,Z_t)$. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] therefore lifts a map $K\to Z$ to a stage, and clause (3) makes two stage maps with the same composite to $Z$ equal after a transition. Fewer than $\kappa$ such choices can be made simultaneously: choose their individual stages and then an upper bound in $T$. Every tail $T_{\geq s}$ has the same filteredness and colimits: a cocone on the tail extends at $t$ using any upper bound of $s,t$, independently of that choice by a further upper bound.

source.place: Lemma A.3.3.17, compactness arguments; Stacks Tag 04AX, categories.tex, section-directed-colimits, elementwise description

proof.text: Apply Step 2 to the maps $a_d:P_d\to F(d)$, obtaining one $s\in T$ and maps $a_{s,d}:P_d\to F_s(d)$ with $x_s(d)a_{s,d}=a_d$. There are fewer than $\kappa$ objects because their identity arrows are distinct. For $t\geq s$ put $a_{t,d}=v_{st}(d)a_{s,d}$ and $H_t(d)=F_t(d)\amalg_{P_d}Q_d$, with legs $i_{t,d}:F_t(d)\to H_t(d)$ and $j_{t,d}:Q_d\to H_t(d)$. The pushout universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] defines transitions $w_{tu,d}$ induced by $v_{tu}(d)$ and $1_{Q_d}$. It also gives $G(d)=\varinjlim_{t\geq s}H_t(d)$ with cocone maps $b_{t,d}$: a compatible family of maps $H_t(d)\to M$ is exactly a map $F(d)\to M$ and a map $Q_d\to M$ agreeing on $P_d$. Each $H_t(d)$ is $\kappa$-presentable, by [lem-coef-ordinary-small-colimit-presentable] for the finite pushout diagram (also an explicit hypothesis of the item). At this point $H_t(d)$ are only separate objectwise presentations, not diagrams in $d$.

source.place: Lemma A.3.3.17, first compactness argument and the displayed objectwise pushout colimit

proof.text: For each $d$ put $R_d=\coprod_{\alpha:e\to d}Q_e$. It is $\kappa$-presentable by [lem-coef-ordinary-small-colimit-presentable], since there are fewer than $\kappa$ arrows of $D$. Map its $\alpha$-summand to $G(d)$ by $Q_e\to G(e)\xrightarrow{G(\alpha)}G(d)$. Step 2 and the presentations of Step 3 give a common $r\geq s$ and factorizations $q_\alpha:Q_e\to H_r(d)$ of these maps. For $t\geq r$ set $q^t_\alpha=w_{rt,d}q_\alpha$. The maps $q_\alpha u_e$ and $i_{r,d}F_r(\alpha)a_{r,e}$ from $P_e$ to $H_r(d)$ agree in $G(d)$: both equal $G(\alpha)f(e)a_e=f(d)F(\alpha)a_e$. Apply Step 2 to each such equality. One upper bound $r_1\geq r$ makes $q^t_\alpha u_e=i_{t,d}F_t(\alpha)a_{t,e}$ for every arrow and every $t\geq r_1$. This uses presentability of $P_e$ and clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise].

source.place: Lemma A.3.3.17, second compactness argument and the first compatibility square, printed pp.883-884

proof.text: For $t\geq r_1$ the equality in Step 4 defines a unique map $A_t(\alpha):H_t(e)\to H_t(d)$ whose restrictions to the pushout legs are $i_{t,d}F_t(\alpha)$ and $q^t_\alpha$. Use [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] twice to compare restrictions to these legs. First, for $t\leq u$ it gives $w_{tu,d}A_t(\alpha)=A_u(\alpha)w_{tu,e}$: on $F_t(e)$ this is naturality of $v_{tu}$, and on $Q_e$ it is $w_{tu,d}q^t_\alpha=q^u_\alpha$. Second, $b_{t,d}A_t(\alpha)=G(\alpha)b_{t,e}$: the $F_t(e)$ restriction is naturality of $f$ and $x_t$, and the $Q_e$ restriction is the chosen factorization of Step 4. These statements hold before imposing any functor laws on $A_t$. In particular all these prospective structure maps extend compatibly when the stage is enlarged.

source.place: Lemma A.3.3.17, construction of prospective structure maps from the first compatibility square

proof.text: At stage $r_1$ compare $A_{r_1}(1_e)j_{r_1,e}$ with $j_{r_1,e}$, and, for every composable $\alpha:e\to d$, $\beta:d\to c$, compare $A_{r_1}(\beta)A_{r_1}(\alpha)j_{r_1,e}$ with $A_{r_1}(\beta\alpha)j_{r_1,e}$. Step 5 and the functor laws in $G$ make each pair equal in the corresponding $G(e)$ or $G(c)$. Their common source $Q_e$ is $\kappa$-presentable. Clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] and Step 2 give a stage $r_2\geq r_1$ where all these equalities hold. There are fewer than $\kappa$ equations, since the set of composable pairs is a subset of $\operatorname{Mor}(D)^2$. Step 5 identifies the transitioned pairs with exactly the analogous pairs for $A_{r_2}$. On the other pushout leg $F_{r_2}(e)$ the same equalities already hold, since $A_{r_2}(\alpha)i_{r_2,e}=i_{r_2,d}F_{r_2}(\alpha)$ and $F_{r_2}$ is a functor. Pushout uniqueness [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] now gives the identity and composition laws on all of $H_{r_2}(e)$. Thus $G_0(d)=H_{r_2}(d)$ and $G_0(\alpha)=A_{r_2}(\alpha)$ define a functor.

source.place: Lemma A.3.3.17, final compactness argument and the second compatibility square, printed p.884; identities made explicit

proof.text: Set $F_0=F_{r_2}$ and $h(d)=i_{r_2,d}$. The restriction formula in Step 5 makes $h:F_0\to G_0$ natural, and the maps $b_{r_2,d}$ form a natural map $b:G_0\to G$. Each $h(d)$ is the pushout of the specified $u_d$ along $a_{r_2,d}$, whose composite with $x_{r_2}(d)$ is $a_d$. The square $(h,x_{r_2},b,f)$ is a pushout pointwise: its iterated pushout is $(F_{r_2}(d)\amalg_{P_d}Q_d)\amalg_{F_{r_2}(d)}F(d)=Q_d\amalg_{P_d}F(d)=G(d)$, with all identifications fixed by their legs. It is a pushout of diagrams as well: for natural maps from $F$ and $G_0$ to a diagram $M$ agreeing on $F_0$, the component pushout properties give unique maps $G(d)\to M(d)$. Their naturality follows by checking on the two pushout legs and applying uniqueness [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Finally $F_0$ is pointwise $\kappa$-presentable by its choice, and $G_0$ is so by Step 3. This proves every clause without canceling any morphism.
